request.name: Tally test 1
request.request:
Write exactly 1 email announcing the launch of this product to people who have not bought it yet - make the case for why it matters now and what to do next.

Tone of voice: Friendly and casual - warm and conversational, like a text from someone the reader trusts.

selected_audience: The ops or no-code person on a small team whose intake form is step one of an automation nobody owns

business.what_it_does: Tally is a form builder that works like a document — you type questions directly on the page and insert blocks (contact info, payments, signatures, file uploads, ratings, etc.) the way you would in Notion, with no coding required.
business.business_model: subscription (freemium — unlimited forms and submissions free, paid Pro and Business tiers for advanced features)

entries.claim: A file upload form lets respondents send files directly without needing to sign up.
entries.verbatim: A file upload form lets you collect files directly from respondents, without the need for them to sign up.

entries.claim: File upload forms are free on all Tally plans, with no limit on the number of files you can collect.
entries.verbatim: File upload forms are free on all Tally plans, with no limit on the number of files you can collect.

entries.claim: The free Tally plan supports individual files up to 10 MB.
entries.verbatim: The free plan supports individual files up to 10 MB.

entries.claim: Tally lets you add a file upload field to any form and start collecting images, PDFs, videos, audio files, and documents in minutes.
entries.verbatim: With Tally, you can add a file upload field to any form and start collecting images, PDFs, videos, audio files, and documents in minutes.

entries.claim: Unlike Google Forms and other tools, Tally respondents don't need to log in to upload files.
entries.verbatim: Unlike Google Forms and other tools, your respondents don’t need to log in to upload files.

entries.claim: Respondents can upload multiple files, with configurable minimum and maximum number of file uploads.
entries.verbatim: If you want respondents to be able to upload multiple files, enable the `Multiple files`option. This will allow you to define the desired `minimum`and `maximum`number of file uploads.

entries.claim: Form builders can enable a Max file size setting so respondents see the file size limit in the upload block.
entries.verbatim: Enable `Max file size` to set a file size limit. Respondents will see the maximum file size limit in the file upload block.

entries.claim: Form builders can restrict uploads to specific allowed file types, such as all image files or just .jpg files.
entries.verbatim: To only accept certain file types, enable `Allowed files` and select the file type(s) you want to accept. For example: - If you only want to accept image files, regardless of the type, select `All image files` - If you only want to accept .jpg files, select `.jpg`

entries.claim: Conditional logic can show or hide the file upload block based on a respondent's previous answers.
entries.verbatim: You can use [conditional logic](https://www.notion.so/6ea9699f446740c8937058ef0dc4dea1) to show or hide the file upload block depending on a respondent's previous answers.

entries.claim: Viewing uploaded files in the Submissions tab requires being logged in to your Tally account.
entries.verbatim: You need to be logged in to your Tally account to view them.

entries.claim: A 'Download file uploads' button lets you batch download all files from a submissions page at once.
entries.verbatim: Use the 'Download file uploads' button at the top of the submissions page to download all files at once.

entries.claim: When exporting file uploads to third-party tools like Google Sheets, an access token is added to the links so files are accessible without being logged into Tally.
entries.verbatim: When you export your file uploads to third-party tools using our integrations, an access token is added to the links, which makes them accessible without the need to be logged in. For example, if you export form submissions to a Google Sheet, anyone with access to that Sheet can click the file upload URL and access the file (without being logged into Tally).

entries.claim: There is no limit to the number of files you can upload or the total storage used.
entries.verbatim: No, there's no limit to the number of files you can upload or the total storage.

entries.claim: Uploaded files are preserved with no time limit as long as the account is open and responses aren't deleted.
entries.verbatim: No, there's no time limit. As long as your account is open and the responses are not deleted from your account, the files are preserved.

entries.claim: Tally was founded in 2020 in Ghent, Belgium by Marie Martens and Filip Minev.
entries.verbatim: Tally was founded in 2020 in Ghent, Belgium by [Marie Martens](https://twitter.com/MarieMartens) and [Filip Minev](https://twitter.com/FilipMinev), with the mission to make form building easy, beautiful, and free.

entries.claim: Tally is completely independent, self-funded, and bootstrapped.
entries.verbatim: The company is completely independent, self-funded and bootstrapped.

entries.claim: Webhooks are available for free to all Tally users.
entries.verbatim: Webhooks are available **for free** to all Tally users.

entries.claim: When a Tally form is submitted, a notification containing the response data is sent to the configured URL in JSON format via a POST request.
entries.verbatim: When someone submits a Tally form, a notification containing the response data gets sent to your URL in **JSON** format via a **POST** request.

entries.claim: Tally webhook endpoints have a 10-second timeout to process and respond to a new submission.
entries.verbatim: A webhook endpoint has a **10-second timeout** to process and respond to a new submission. If the processing takes longer, it's advisable to call another service internally.

entries.claim: Tally webhook requests can include a Tally-Signature header containing a SHA256 cryptographic hash of the payload for verification.
entries.verbatim: When this option is enabled, the webhook requests will contain a `Tally-Signature` header. The value of this header is a SHA256 cryptographic hash of the webhook payload.

entries.claim: Tally supports connecting unlimited webhook URLs, which can be paused via a toggle.
entries.verbatim: You can connect unlimited webhook URLs and pause them by clicking the toggle.

entries.claim: If a webhook delivery fails, Tally retries after 5 minutes, then 30 minutes, then 1 hour, then 6 hours, then 1 day.
entries.verbatim: 1. The first retry occurs after 5 minutes 2. If the first retry fails, the second retry is scheduled after 30 minutes 3. If the second retry fails, the third retry is scheduled after 1 hour 4. If the third retry fails, the fourth retry is scheduled after 6 hours 5. If the fourth retry fails, the fifth retry is scheduled after 1 day

entries.claim: If all retries fail, Tally sends a one-time email to the form owner and creator with the reason and a link to fix it.
entries.verbatim: If all retries fail, we'll also send a one-time email to the form owner and creator with the reason and a link to fix it. We won't email again for the same failure until it resolves and happens again.

entries.claim: Webhooks created via an integration can only be removed from within that integration.
entries.verbatim: If the webhook is created from an [integration](https://tally.so/help/integrations), then you can only remove the webhook in the integration where you originally created it.

entries.claim: Tally offers integrations with Zapier, Make, Pipedream, and Integrately for syncing form submissions.
entries.verbatim: If you're instead looking for a non-technical way to sync Tally form submissions with other apps, check out our [Zapier](/help/zapier-integration), [Make](/help/make-integration), [Pipedream](/help/pipedream-integration) or [Integrately](/help/integrately-integration) integrations.

entries.claim: Tally offers an MCP server for AI agents and tools like Claude, requiring no endpoints or JSON.
entries.verbatim: If you’re building with AI agents or tools like Claude, check out the [Tally MCP server](/help/mcp). No endpoints or JSON required.

entries.claim: A webhook lets you send every form submission as structured JSON to any HTTP endpoint in real time.
entries.verbatim: A webhook lets you send every form submission as structured JSON to any HTTP endpoint in real time.

entries.claim: Instead of polling the Tally API or exporting CSVs, webhooks push data the moment a form is submitted.
entries.verbatim: Instead of polling the Tally API or exporting CSVs, webhooks push data the moment a form is submitted.

entries.claim: A Tally form can trigger automation platforms like Make, Zapier, or n8n, which then route the data to CRMs, billing tools, internal databases, or messaging apps.
entries.verbatim: A Tally form can trigger automation platforms like [Make](/help/make-integration), [Zapier](/help/zapier-integration) or [n8n](/help/n8n-integration), which then route the data to CRMs, billing tools, internal databases or messaging apps.

entries.claim: Tally can sign each webhook request with a SHA256 signature so you can verify that the payload really came from Tally before you process it.
entries.verbatim: Tally can sign each webhook request with a SHA256 signature so you can verify that the payload really came from Tally before you process it.

entries.claim: You can list delivery events, inspect responses and retry failed webhook attempts, which makes production workflows much easier to monitor and debug.
entries.verbatim: You can list delivery events, inspect responses and retry failed webhook attempts, which makes production workflows much easier to monitor and debug.

segments.name: The ops or no-code person on a small team whose intake form is step one of an automation nobody owns
segments.situation: They inherited the form. It feeds something — a CRM record, a Slack channel, a billing step, an onboarding checklist — and the handoff between the form and the rest of the stack is currently a human. Someone exports a CSV on Mondays, or a scheduled job polls an API, or the form emails a shared inbox and a person retypes it. They have built the downstream half already in Make, Zapier or n8n and they are competent enough to read webhook docs, which means their evaluation is not about whether a form is pretty. It is about whether a delivery that fails at 2am gets retried, whether they will find out when it doesn't, whether they can verify a payload came from the vendor before it writes to a production database, and whether the vendor will move webhooks behind a seat-priced tier the quarter after they standardise on it. The failure they fear is specific and quiet: the form keeps accepting submissions and the records stop appearing.
segments.job_to_be_done: Wants the webhook to send a conditional response or redirect back to the respondent based on their form answers, rather than only the platform's own generic acknowledgement.
segments.trigger: Testing a newly built scenario with a manual 'Run once' before going live, and finding the instant webhook trigger does not surface any existing submissions until a new one arrives.; Building or replacing a form-to-CRM workflow is the point where someone decides to add a validation step, because the templates in circulation write everything through unchecked.

pains.statement: After a Tally form submits to a webhook, the respondent cannot be reliably redirected or shown a conditional response from the automation tool; the connection appears to be lost once the platform returns its own 'accepted' acknowledgement.

pains.statement: Common form-to-CRM automation patterns write submissions directly into the contact database without checking for typos, blank required fields, or bot spam, so bad records accumulate and must be cleaned up by hand afterward.

provenance.quote: Typos, blank names and bot spam land in your contact database, and somebody cleans it up by hand later.

segments.name: A freelance designer or one-person studio who spends the first two weeks of every project chasing brand assets out of a client's inbox
segments.situation: Every new engagement starts the same way: they need the logo in a usable format, the old brand guidelines PDF, photography the client owns, a rough brief, the billing details and whoever's sign-off they'll need later. None of it arrives in one place. It comes back as a reply-all thread, a file-transfer link that expires before they've downloaded it, a shared-drive invite the client's IT blocks, and a 'can you just pull it off our website?'. They almost certainly have a form somewhere already — a Google Form, a free Typeform, a page on their Squarespace site — and each one failed in its own way: the client couldn't upload without signing into an account, or the packaged InDesign file was too big for the free tier, or the form itself carried someone else's logo at the bottom, which reads badly on the one document where they are selling their own taste in branding. They are not short of tooling and they are not technical; they are short of a single link they can paste into a kickoff email and trust. If the brief is thin, the first round of work is wrong, and the rework is unbilled.

segments.name: An indie SaaS founder or creator who keeps shipping features without knowing whether anyone asked for them
segments.situation: They are the product person, the support inbox and the release notes. Feedback reaches them as fragments: a Discord message, a churn email with no reason given, three support threads that turn out to be the same confusion. Bug reports arrive as 'it's broken on my end' with no screenshot and no browser, so every one costs a round trip. They have tried asking — an in-app link, a tweet, a survey emailed to their list — and the survey either died at a low response rate or hit a free-tier response cap partway through a run, which means the data they do have is a self-selected slice of their loudest users. Meanwhile the team, if there is a team, lives in Notion and Slack, and anything that lands in a separate dashboard nobody opens is effectively unread. The cost is not a number they track; it is a roadmap argued from anecdote and a quarter spent on the wrong thing.

objections.objection: The free plan already does everything I need, so why would I ever pay — and if I never pay, you have no business asking me to.
objections.answer: This is self-inflicted and the honest answer is narrow: the vendor's own claim is that 99% of features are free (E111), so the paid upgrade is not 'more form builder'. Pro is for a specific short list — removing Tally's branding (E296), hosting on your own subdomain (E297), unlimited team members in shared workspaces (E298), workspaces and folders with access rights (E305), partial submissions (E299), drop-off analytics (E308), version history to 30 days (E309), and removing the 10 MB per-file ceiling (E306, E252). Cancel anytime (E242) makes it a per-project expense rather than a commitment. Nothing in the evidence quantifies the value of any of these, so copy that promises ROI here is unsupported.

objections.objection: Your own pages do not agree on what Pro costs. The pricing page says €20/month, the help pages say $29/month, and the comparison table prices custom domains at $29 and data retention at $89 while the plan page says Business is €65. If I cannot trust the price I cannot trust the plan.
objections.answer: Nothing in the supplied evidence resolves this. E270 (€20) and E271 (€65) come from the pricing page; E241 ($29/$290) and E259 ($89/$890) from the plan help pages; E68, E72, E76 and E102 repeat the dollar figures in the comparison material. There is no dated or canonical price in the ledger, so the conflict cannot be answered with what we know — it must be checked with the client before any email names a number.

objections.objection: 'Free forever' from a bootstrapped startup is a promise with a clock on it. You will get acquired, or raise prices, or decide my usage is no longer 'fair usage' — and by then my forms are embedded on client sites.
objections.answer: Partly answerable. They are independent, self-funded and bootstrapped with no outside investors (E20, E175, E178), have been going since 2020 (E19), are funded by customers rather than a runway, build in public with a public roadmap and documented milestones (E176, E177), and are at 500,000+ teams (E273, E320), which is the only durability signal in the ledger. The 'fair usage' half is not answered: the free offer is explicitly conditional on fair usage guidelines (E272, E328, E186) and the only ledger entry for the policy itself is a bare link (E160) with no stated thresholds. We cannot tell a reader where the line is.

objections.objection: I already have Google Forms in my Workspace and a Typeform the last person set up. Switching is a week of rebuilding forms that currently work, and re-embedding them everywhere they are embedded.
objections.answer: Partly answerable. Forms import in one click (E92), and the importer takes forms from other tools or even from a screenshot or PDF (E219); embedding works on WordPress, Webflow, Framer, Notion and any other site builder (E359, E220). On the 'why bother' half, the vendor's own comparison is the argument: respondents do not need to log in to upload files (E5), Google Forms has no custom domains (E71), no branding removal (E75), no formula editor (E59), no PDF export of submissions (E67), limited conditional logic (E55) and payments only via third parties (E63), while Typeform's free tier caps at 10 responses a month (E41) and charges for file uploads and payments (E49, E61). What the evidence does not cover: whether existing form URLs, embed snippets or historical responses survive a migration.

provenance.source: Compare Tally: Free Form Builder vs Typeform, Jotform & More (https://tally.so/help/compare)
provenance.quote: [Tally](https://tally.so) stands out as the only form builder offering unlimited forms and unlimited submissions completely free, but how does it compare to popular alternatives like Typeform, Jotform, Google Forms, and other competitors?

objections.objection: A free tool will make me look cheap in front of my clients. The form is the first thing they see from me and it will have your name on it.
objections.answer: Answerable, but only on the paid tier: Pro hides all branding (E296, E243), hosts forms on your own subdomain for branded links (E297, E362, E244), lets you set the OG image, favicon, title and description so the link preview is yours (E304, E253), and allows custom CSS and built-in design control (E301, E300, E248). For borrowed credibility: 500,000+ teams including Notion, Make, Buy Me a Coffee, Rakuten and Glovo (E273, E274, E275, E276, E277, E278), Dribbble's Director of Advertising on choosing it for community surveys (E269), a Product Hunt Golden Kitty (E326), and press in Fast Company and The Brand Identity (E179, E180).

objections.objection: I cannot put candidate CVs, signed contracts or client data into a tool I have not vetted. Legal will ask where it is hosted, what the DPA says, and whether you have a security certification.
objections.answer: Strong on residency and weak on paperwork. Belgium-based EU company, GDPR compliant, all form data stored in Europe (E315, E376, E329, E97, E98, E330), encrypted in transit and at rest with stated control over what you collect (E316, E332), no cookie-tracking (E331), password protection and two-factor authentication on free plans (E99, E100, E207), reCAPTCHA (E204), and on Business automatic deletion of submissions after a set period for privacy compliance (E311, E261, E163, E317). What is missing from the evidence entirely: SOC 2 or ISO certification, a signable DPA, sub-processor list, or any audit. If the reader's blocker is procurement paperwork rather than hosting location, we cannot answer it.

objections.objection: We are a team, not a solo creator. Shared ownership, access control and someone overwriting a live form are my actual problems, and this looks like a tool for one person.
objections.answer: Answerable. Unlimited team members in shared workspaces (E298, E245, E155), forms grouped into workspaces and folders with managed team access rights (E305, E246), version history to restore a form 30 days back on Pro and 90 on Business (E309, E251, E313, E263), and webhook failures email both the form owner and the creator rather than one person (E27). Proof that teams at scale run on it: Notion, Make, Rakuten, Glovo (E274–E278), 500,000+ teams (E320), and the Make customer story on using a Tally form inside Customer Success (E264).

objections.objection: I could build this myself. A form page and an endpoint is an afternoon, and then I own it.
objections.answer: Answerable on the unglamorous half they are not costing in: delivery retries on a stated schedule — 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day (E26); a one-time email to owner and creator when all retries fail, with the reason and a link to fix it (E27); SHA256 request signing via a Tally-Signature header so payloads can be verified before processing (E24, E34); a delivery event log with response inspection and manual retry (E35); unlimited webhook URLs with pause toggles (E25); a documented 10-second endpoint timeout (E23); and all of it free (E21). Plus the parts they would not build: 50+ languages and RTL (E358, E217), accessibility on semantic HTML with keyboard and screen-reader support on every plan (E93, E94, E95, E96), PDF generation per submission (E36, E218), and an MCP server and Claude connector (E30, E239, E222).

objections.objection: If it is genuinely unlimited and free, something must be worse — support, limits you have not published, or a product that stops being developed.
objections.answer: Partial. Not answered: support response times or staffing, and the fair-usage thresholds (E160) that the whole free offer is conditioned on.

# File upload forms
A file upload form lets you collect files directly from respondents, without the need for them to sign up. With Tally, you can add a file upload field to any form and start collecting images, PDFs, videos, audio files, and documents in minutes. You can allow multiple file uploads, define the file types and set size limits to match your needs. File upload forms are free on all Tally plans, with no limit on the number of files you can collect.

![Create a form with a file upload](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F3afc7cd1-28d8-46a1-9953-efe0e1d4e19c%2FTally_File_Upload.jpg?table=block&id=d03102a0-a2af-4e8d-aafb-0b9153142005&cache=v2)

![File uploads are free for all Tally users. The free plan supports individual files up to 10 MB. Upgrade to Tally Pro to collect files of any size without limits.](https://app.notion.com/icons/gift_green.svg?mode=light)

File uploads are free for all Tally users. The free plan supports individual files up to 10 MB. Upgrade to [Tally Pro](https://tally.so/help/tally-pro) to collect files of any size without limits.

---

[Why use Tally for file upload forms?](#3368a570dd6a80ba929cf1e7ce6996b7)[How to add a build a file upload form (without login)](#3bcd712e81334fc8a8fd50d36a00e7ba)[File upload settings](#068ae965412343a2bfb9ff490b972e58)[Allow multiple file uploads](#642c932f2b7146019995d08bf6eca38c)[Set a maximum file size](#7d58edb054f547ee9f84854482cbaae1)[Restrict file types](#22f01d767a0146cbac61dfc73cb323f3)[Show or hide based on answers](#06d44474d058483b8ad169cc745271ff)[Accessing and downloading uploaded files](#3368a570dd6a80e898acda951b930de7)[Free file upload form templates](#d2ca6abcb35844ea94e156c0ea609427)[Frequently Asked Questions](#16ae3a3959fd4cbeb9ee38a6b7c1ad40)[Do more with Tally](#3b28a570dd6a80f98e73ec3c5b6e470f)

---

### **Why use Tally for file upload forms?**
- **No sign-in required**
  Unlike Google Forms and other tools, your respondents don’t need to log in to upload files. No Google account and login required.

- **Affordable file uploads**
  File uploads are often locked behind expensive plans in other tools. With Tally, you get file uploads up to 10MB per file for free, without paying enterprise-level prices just to collect files. [Tally Pro](/help/tally-pro) removes the 10MB file size limit per file at $29/month.

- **Your data is stored securely**
  Tally is based in Europe and complies with the [GDPR framework](/help/gdpr).

### How to add a build a file upload form (without login)
Type `/file` to insert a file upload block. Respondents can click to choose a file or directly drag files into the file upload block.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2Fd2987fff-6222-4c25-b75f-6951cc596d24%2FFile-upload-1.png?table=block&id=27358ba9-0018-49f1-8ad8-dcdadced8c4d&cache=v2)

### File upload settings
Click `::` to open the file upload settings. You can:

- Make the file upload required or optional

- Allow multiple files (and set a minimum and maximum number of files)

- Set a maximum file size

- Define the allowed file types

- Hide a block (and show it with [conditional logic](/help/conditional-form-logic))

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2Fa75aa45c-3e74-4904-86ca-eb54adb2675f%2FFile-upload-2.png?table=block&id=13ea1b98-a12e-4da3-ad4b-69bf20f1e0f9&cache=v2)

#### Allow multiple file uploads
If you want respondents to be able to upload multiple files, enable the `Multiple files`option. This will allow you to define the desired `minimum`and `maximum`number of file uploads.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F32f7b0d2-9e7e-4b51-8e4f-50bb3274dfe9%2FFile-upload-3.png?table=block&id=ae211290-967c-48d1-884e-ef09a2a99f60&cache=v2)

Respondents can drag multiple files at once in the file upload block or upload them one by one, using the `Upload another file` button.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F5827ef3c-1622-4856-8c16-c475b07dde2b%2FFile-upload-4.png?table=block&id=cac2a5c0-ab98-42ce-a4d3-6c05161e8865&cache=v2)

#### Set a maximum file size
Enable `Max file size` to set a file size limit. Respondents will see the maximum file size limit in the file upload block.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2Ffce71b96-fd50-4c16-95e7-90de460ed669%2FFile-upload-5.png?table=block&id=d8a3853e-c0c2-411f-96cb-104a9a338ceb&cache=v2)

![Tally allows file uploads with an individual size of 10MB for free. To collect larger files, upgrade to Tally Pro.](https://app.notion.com/icons/flash_pink.svg?mode=light)

Tally allows file uploads with an individual size of **10MB for free**. To collect larger files, upgrade to [Tally Pro](/help/tally-pro).

#### Restrict file types
To only accept certain file types, enable `Allowed files` and select the file type(s) you want to accept. For example:

- If you only want to accept image files, regardless of the type, select `All image files`

- If you only want to accept .jpg files, select `.jpg`

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F564a6e4e-2959-4388-9afa-674bd6f70e7f%2FFile-upload-6.png?table=block&id=42f45c69-f489-4450-9916-18842321d296&cache=v2)

Respondents will see the required file type(s) indicated in the file upload block.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F69cd9fac-5736-4d07-8bfc-f21938db93d2%2FFile-upload-7.png?table=block&id=e8798d6e-ddff-4904-9b9e-51e32232e50d&cache=v2)

#### Show or hide based on answers
You can use [conditional logic](https://www.notion.so/6ea9699f446740c8937058ef0dc4dea1) to show or hide the file upload block depending on a respondent's previous answers. For example, only ask for a portfolio if someone selects "Freelancer" as their role, or only request a doctor's note if a respondent confirms a medical absence.

### Accessing and downloading uploaded files
All uploaded files are stored securely and accessible from the `Submissions` tab of your form. They can be accessed through an authenticated link or downloaded directly to your device.

- **View files:** Open any submission to preview or access uploaded files. You need to be logged in to your Tally account to view them.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2Fad32bc82-d1d9-4f9c-b12d-2789c73de35d%2FAuthenticated_file_upload_URLS.png?table=block&id=673a18a5-6d9c-43f4-b50a-ed234ee04c54&cache=v2)

- **Download individual files:** Click the download icon next to any file within a submission.

- **Batch download:** Use the 'Download file uploads' button at the top of the submissions page to download all files at once. If your form submissions span multiple pages, you'll need to repeat this step on each page to download all files.

![notion image](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F23e6680b-4a09-4e46-b05c-cbdcd595bdef%2FCleanShot_2024-04-22_at_20.08.522x.png?table=block&id=cbb4ffb7-7d43-4f2f-8782-13fd21bb93b4&cache=v2)

![When you export your file uploads to third-party tools using our integrations, an access token is added to the links, which makes them accessible without the need to be logged in. For example, if you export form submissions to a Google Sheet, anyone with access to that Sheet can click the file upload URL and access the file (without being logged into Tally).](https://app.notion.com/icons/info-alternate_blue.svg?mode=light)

When you export your file uploads to third-party tools using our integrations, an access token is added to the links, which makes them accessible without the need to be logged in. For example, if you export form submissions to a Google Sheet, anyone with access to that Sheet can click the file upload URL and access the file (without being logged into Tally).

### Free file upload form templates
Not sure where to start? These free Tally templates already include a file upload field — just open, customize, and share.

- **[Job Application Form](https://tally.so/templates/job-application-form/vmZVmD)****:** Collect resumes, cover letters, and candidate details in one place. Ideal for hiring teams and recruiters.

- **[Bug Report Form](https://tally.so/templates/customer-support-template/3xJBon)****:** Let users attach screenshots or screen recordings alongside their bug report. Built for SaaS and product teams.

- **[Client Intake Form](https://tally.so/templates/client-intake-form/w2rgew)****:** Gather project briefs, reference files, and onboarding details from new clients. Great for freelancers and agencies.

- **[Branding Project Intake Form](https://tally.so/templates/branding-project-intake-form-template/mZNovm)****:** Collect brand assets, design inspiration, and creative direction from clients before kicking off a project.

Browse all [Tally form templates](https://tally.so/templates) to find more.

### Frequently Asked Questions
**Can I create a file upload form without login?**

Yes. Unlike with Google Forms, respondents can upload files without signing up for Tally or creating any kind of account.

**What is the maximum file size I can upload with a free Tally account?**

With a free account, the maximum file size you can upload is 10MB. However, if you have a [Pro account](/help/tally-pro), there's no limit to the file upload size.

**How many files can I upload? Is there a limit to the total weight of the files?**

No, there's no limit to the number of files you can upload or the total storage. However, please note that you must respect our [Fair Use Policy](/help/fair-use-policy).

**Is there a time limit for how long my files are stored in the system?**

No, there's no time limit. As long as your account is open and the responses are not deleted from your account, the files are preserved.

**Do I need to respect any usage guidelines?**

Yes, as a user of our service, you must respect our [Fair Use Policy.](/help/fair-use-policy) This policy helps us maintain the quality and integrity of our service for all users.

### Do more with Tally

### Tagline
[Tally](https://tally.so) is the simplest way to create forms, for free.

### **Short Description**
Say goodbye to boring forms. Meet Tally — the free, intuitive form builder you’ve been looking for.

### **Boilerplate Description**
Tally is a simple, yet powerful form builder that allows you to create any type of form without breaking the bank. Creators and teams use Tally to kickstart their business, validate ideas, gather customer feedback, perform market research or sell products.

- **Works like a doc:** Just start typing and use shortcuts to create any type of form in seconds.

- **Unlimited forms & responses for free:** Tally is the only form builder out there that offers unlimited forms, responses and advanced features for free.

- **Tally Pro:** 99% of the features are available for free, combined with an empowering [Pro plan](/help/tally-pro) aimed at the needs of creators & teams such as team collaboration, custom domains, removal of Tally branding, and more.

Tally was founded in 2020 in Ghent, Belgium by [Marie Martens](https://twitter.com/MarieMartens) and [Filip Minev](https://twitter.com/FilipMinev), with the mission to make form building easy, beautiful, and free. The company is completely independent, self-funded and bootstrapped.

# Compare form builders
Choosing the right form builder can transform how you collect data, generate leads, and engage with your audience. [Tally](https://tally.so) stands out as the only form builder offering unlimited forms and unlimited submissions completely free, but how does it compare to popular alternatives like Typeform, Jotform, Google Forms, and other competitors?

Explore our detailed comparisons below to see how Tally stacks up against each major form builder, complete with feature tables, pricing breakdowns, user reviews, and real-world use cases.

---

[![Tally, a powerful Notion Forms alternative](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F42c71e43-bd5f-4a60-9f04-9fe93970cb8e%2FNotion-logo.svg.png?table=block&id=12a8a570-dd6a-8022-a601-c99bc359749a&cache=v2)

Tally, a free Formstack alternative](/help/tally-a-free-formstack-alternative)

---

Unlike competitors that lock essential features behind expensive paywalls or limit monthly responses, Tally provides a truly free solution with professional features included. From [conditional logic](/help/conditional-form-logic) and [file uploads](/help/file-uploads) to [payment processing](/help/payment-forms) and [custom domains](/help/custom-domains), discover how Tally delivers enterprise-grade functionality without the enterprise price tag.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Feature | Tally | Typeform | Jotform | Google Forms |
| **Free Plan** | ✅ Unlimited | ❌ 10 responses/mo | ❌ 100 responses/mo | ✅ Unlimited |
| **Unlimited Responses** | ✅ Free | ❌ $39+/mo | ❌ $34+/mo | ✅ Free |
| **File Uploads** | ✅ Free (10MB/file) | ❌ $39+/mo | ❌ $34+/mo | ✅ Free (limited) |
| **Conditional Logic** | ✅ Free | ✅ Free | ❌ $34+/mo | ✅ Limited |
| **Formula editor** | ✅ Free | ❌ $59/mo | ⚠️ Widget only | ❌ No |
| **Accept Payments** | ✅ Free | ❌ $39+/mo | ❌ $34+/mo | ❌ Third-party only |
| **Export submissions as PDF** | ✅ Free | ❌ No | ✅ Free | ❌ No |
| **Custom Domains** | ✅ $29/mo | ❌ $99+/mo | ❌ $39+/mo | ❌ No |
| **Remove Branding** | ✅ $29/mo | ✅ $79/mo | ✅ $34/mo | ❌ No |
| **Submissions data retention** | ✅ $89/mo | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** | ✅ Free | ✅ Free | ✅ Free | ❌ No |
| **AI form builder** | ✅ Free | ❌ $39+/mo | ✅ Free | ❌ $14+/mo |
| **User Rating** | 4.8/5 | 4.5/5 | 4.4/5 | 4.6/5 |

---

### Frequently Asked Questions About Form Builder Comparisons
**Q: Which form builder is completely free?**
A: Google Forms and Tally both offer truly free plans with unlimited submissions. However, Tally provides significantly more advanced features on its free plan, including file uploads, conditional logic, payment processing, and [customization options](/help/customize-your-form) that Google Forms lacks.

**Q: Is Tally better than Typeform?**
A: For most users, yes. Tally offers unlimited forms and responses for free, while Typeform limits free users to 10 responses per month. Tally also includes many features (file uploads, payments, custom domains) that require expensive Typeform upgrades.

**Q: What's the cheapest form builder with unlimited responses?**
A: Tally offers unlimited responses [completely free](https://tally.so/pricing). If you need premium features, Tally Pro at $29/month is more affordable than Typeform ($39/mo for only 100 responses), Jotform ($34/mo for 1,000 responses), or Paperform ($20/mo with limits).

**Q: Can I switch form builders easily?**
A: You can [import your forms](/help/import) into Tally in one click.

**Q: Which form builder is best for small businesses?**
A: Tally is ideal for small businesses because it provides unlimited usage and professional features without subscription costs. As you grow, affordable upgrades add team collaboration and advanced customization without breaking the budget.

**Q: Are free form builders secure?**
A: Yes, reputable free form builders like Tally, Google Forms, and Typeform implement strong security measures. Tally is hosted in the EU, [GDPR-compliant](/help/gdpr), and offers features like password protection and two-factor authentication even on free plans.

**Q: What’s the best form builder to create professional forms?**
A: Tally is increasingly popular among developers, marketers, and product teams for its flexibility, customizability and value for money. Typeform remains popular for its specific format (one question per page). Jotform is common in enterprise settings with complex requirements, but not known for design flexibility.

**Q: Are Tally forms accessible?**
A: Yes. Tally forms are designed with accessibility in mind — built on semantic HTML, they can be completed using keyboard navigation and screen readers like VoiceOver and NVDA, on every plan, for free. Read more about [how Tally approaches accessibility](https://app.notion.com/p/37a8a570dd6a81aea931d5c282c43749).

documents.title: About Tally: Meet the Team Behind the Form Builder
documents.content:
# The story of Tally
Forms have been around since the beginning of the internet. And somehow, they’ve stayed complicated, expensive, and boring to build. We thought that didn’t make sense, so we built [Tally](https://tally.so): a form builder that doesn’t break the bank and feels as simple as writing a document.

From day one, we wanted Tally to feel different. Not just easier, but better. More fun to use. More flexible. Software you actually enjoy opening, not something you tolerate.

We believe tools should empower you and your work. Not limit you with features locked behind paywalls or constant nudges to upgrade. Good tools should be accessible, generous, and grow with you. That’s why Tally is free for most use cases, and stays affordable when you need more.

We’re a small, independent team based in Europe, bootstrapped and funded by our customers. That gives us the freedom to build the product the way we think it should be built. We care about the long term. About building something opinionated, focused, and something people genuinely love to use.

Tally is our take on what form building should feel like.

We hope you enjoy what we’re building.

— Team Tally

![page icon](https://app.notion.com/image/attachment%3A0ab0122b-5354-4617-9a36-47194ab66f53%3AFrame_14.png?table=block&id=32d8a570-dd6a-8084-aa9a-e6f30d7095f2&cache=v2)

**We build in public**

Every milestone is documented on [blog.tally.so](https://blog.tally.so).

![page icon](https://app.notion.com/image/attachment%3Ae02e314c-a25b-4281-81d8-363233f0d061%3AFrame_17.png?table=block&id=32d8a570-dd6a-80a6-b27e-c9c18503c175&cache=v2)

documents.content:
# Tally Features
We provide unlimited forms, submissions, and everything you need to create professional forms and surveys, all free of charge as long as you stay within our [fair usage guidelines](https://tally.so/help/fair-use-policy). In need of that little bit extra? Our [Pro](/help/tally-pro) and [Business](/help/tally-business) plan offer empowering features tailored to the advanced needs of teams and creators.

**✔ Create unlimited forms for free**

**✔ Collect unlimited submissions for free**

**✔ Add free logic and calculations**

**✔ Customize your form for free**

![Tally features](https://app.notion.com/image/https%3A%2F%2Fprod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com%2Fc7def46e-5b1b-431a-b65a-93222e53bf0d%2F6fa70a5a-42e0-4cda-99aa-a9ba09a3b6f6%2FTally_pricing.png?table=block&id=4a6f5de9-a3ca-4b3e-a461-ec2c98e212d8&cache=v2)

![Create a free form, no sign-up required.

**[Create a free form](https://tally.so/create)****, no sign-up required.**

## Questions & answers
Is Tally really free?

Yes! Born out of frustration with expensive form builders, Tally offers unlimited forms and submissions for free within our [fair use guidelines](/help/fair-use-policy). You can [get started right away](/create) and create forms using advanced features like [conditional logic](/help/conditional-form-logic), [signatures](/help/electronic-signatures), [calculations](/help/form-calculator), [file uploads](/help/file-uploads), and many more — all for free and without time restrictions.

Are Tally forms secure?

Yes, Tally takes security seriously. As a Belgium-based (EU) company, we fully comply with [GDPR requirements](/help/gdpr) and store all form data in Europe. Unlike most form builders that limit submissions or restrict advanced features to premium plans, Tally offers unlimited forms and submissions for free. How can I get started?

You can start creating your first form right away—no sign up needed! [Create your first form here](/create) or head over to our [signup page](/signup) to create your account. For tips and best practices, check out our [Get started guide](/help/create-a-form).

Click me
